reason: The goal is to supply fuel, and sugar is the only offered combination.
expectation: The muscle fibers will receive sugar as fuel, though they may still need oxygen.

effect: The fibers process sugar in the cell fluid, producing some ATP and sending processed fuel into mitochondria; I expect oxygen is the next supply.
reaction: The split path is interesting, though the picture alone leaves the details unclear.
reason: Oxygen is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining supply in the goal.
expectation: The fibers will use oxygen with the processed fuel to support further ATP production.

effect: The result shows ATP being remade using fuel and oxygen, then used for muscle work; the next goal is to collect the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: The ATP cycle makes the running cost clearer.
reason: Wrapping the fibers is the only offered combination and seems useful for grouping their pulls.
expectation: The wrapping will bundle the muscle fibers so their pulls can be collected, perhaps ready for tendon attachment.

effect: The wrapping grouped the muscle cells into bundles, with their ends still available for tendon attachment.
reaction: The shared sleeve makes the grouping easy to picture.
reason: I want to attach a tendon to transmit the bundles’ pull; I’ll start with the front tendons.
expectation: The front tendons will attach to the muscle bundles, forming a group that can transmit their pull.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons also seem suitable, but I have no clear reason to choose them first.

effect: The front tendons formed bending muscles, and the result explains that tendons transmit their pull to an attachment.
reaction: The link to moving a joint makes the tendons’ purpose clearer.
reason: The rear tendons are the only offered combination and should complete the other muscle group.
expectation: The rear tendons will attach to muscle bundles to form a second muscle group, perhaps one that straightens the joint.

effect: The rear tendons formed straightening muscles, completing the two muscle groups and the chapter goal.
reaction: The paired bending and straightening groups make me curious how they will move a joint together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile because the result connected fuel, ATP and muscle work in a clear cycle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the second set of tendons felt somewhat repetitive after making the first muscle group, although it completed the pair.

surprise.text: I was interested that sugar processing was shown both producing some ATP in the cell fluid and sending processed fuel to mitochondria.

arbitrary.text: Choosing the front tendons first felt arbitrary because both tendon options seemed equally suitable and I had no reason to prefer one.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the opposing muscle groups attach to bones and work together at a joint.
